human_name: Modular gap certificates exclude bounded denominators
claim_ceiling: A finite denominator exclusion only; the first rung uses a low-carry bottom band, while the large rungs use arbitrary Farey-neighbour gaps. No irrationality conclusion.
core_idea: Assume a rational presentation with bounded reduced denominator, clear it at a selected binary scale, and use an exact certified modular gap to contradict integrality.
invariant: After denominator clearing, the certified residue or Farey interval remains disjoint from the integer lattice.
transformation: Convert a candidate rational denominator bound into a finite certificate search at a compatible dyadic scale, then transport the exclusion through exact Lambert-form identities.
observable_controlled: The reduced denominator of any rational representation of the binary totient series.
proves_when_hypotheses_hold: No rational presentation exists with denominator at or below the certificate's explicit bound; transported formulations inherit the corresponding bound.
sharp_failures: Z01::totient_denominator_exclusion_ladder is bounded: no finite residue certificate alone excludes all possible rational denominators.

human_name: Odd-core basis for dyadic totient sections
claim_ceiling: A basis and relation classification for dyadic totient sections, not irrationality of the evaluated series.
core_idea: Use the two elementary two-adic scaling identities to reduce every dyadic section to odd-core channels, then prove those channels linearly independent by finite-level separation.
invariant: Odd-core channels have distinct finite-level signatures that survive passage to the full family.
transformation: Normalize arbitrary dyadic sections to odd-core representatives and lift finite linear independence through finite character.
observable_controlled: The rational span and all rational linear relations of the full dyadic totient kernel.
proves_when_hypotheses_hold: The odd-core family is an explicit basis and the only full-kernel relations are generated by the elementary scaling identities.
sharp_failures: Z09::full_dyadic_kernel_infinite_dimensional is coefficient-sequence structure and does not itself imply irrationality of the evaluated series.

human_name: Scalar localisation transfers denominator height into coefficients
claim_ceiling: Pointwise scalar and rational-linear divisibility only; a uniform obstruction follows only along a family whose complementary denominator factor is proved unbounded.
core_idea: Clearing part of a rational denominator cannot erase arithmetic height: the complementary factor must divide the scalar coefficient.
invariant: The reduced numerator-denominator coprimality forces any cleared complementary denominator into the multiplier.
transformation: Factor the reduced denominator into the part cleared by H and its complement, then classify rational-linear descenders as scalar evaluation channels.
observable_controlled: The minimum coefficient height required by scalar denominator-clearing arguments.
proves_when_hypotheses_hold: A scalar or rational-linear clearing route relocates the discarded denominator into the coefficient; along any family with unbounded complementary factor, uniformly small coefficients are impossible.
sharp_failures: linearDescender_eq_smul_eval classifies rational-linear single-scalar channels only; nonlinear and genuinely multivariable routes remain outside its scope.

claim_ceiling: An exact coefficient-dilation identity for arbitrary support and its prime-support specialization; no universal irrationality conclusion.
core_idea: When a support element dilates an index, separate the inherited divisors, the new dilator itself, and the genuinely composite cross-divisors.
invariant: Every support divisor of a*x belongs to exactly one of the inherited, new-element, or defect classes.
transformation: Partition the divisor-incidence count under multiplication by a support element and expose the extra defect term explicitly.
observable_controlled: The change in support coefficient under multiplicative dilation.
proves_when_hypotheses_hold: The exact coefficient identity remains valid for arbitrary support; on prime support the defect vanishes and the prime-dilation formula is recovered.
sharp_failures: supportCoeff_mul_prime_support cannot be transported unchanged to composite support; supportCoeff_mul_eq_add_defect records the missing term.

human_name: Prime support cancels the dilation defect
claim_ceiling: Prime-only support; composite supports require the explicit defect-accounting repair.
core_idea: When every support element is prime, a divisor of a*x that is neither inherited from x nor equal to a cannot remain inside the support, so the composite defect vanishes.
invariant: Prime support excludes composite cross-divisors from the support-incidence count.
transformation: Specialise the exact composite-defect identity to a prime-only support and discharge the defect term as zero.
observable_controlled: The support coefficient after multiplying an index by a support prime.
proves_when_hypotheses_hold: The arbitrary-support dilation identity collapses to the prime-dilation formula.
sharp_failures: supportCoeff_mul_eq_add_defect shows that dropping prime support restores a possibly nonzero composite defect.

human_name: Self-absorbing divisor bounds force sublogarithmic zero windows
claim_ceiling: A necessary zero-window bound under an assumed rational value. The theorem supplies B after A and p are fixed; the proof term chooses B from epsilon, c and v, but the exported binder order does not provide one common B across all A and p.
core_idea: Under a rational-value hypothesis, a long coefficient-zero window creates too many divisibility obligations; choosing an auxiliary parameter absorbs the window length into the logarithmic bound.
invariant: The displayed rational denominator is fixed while a zero window forces a growing family of divisors into a controlled integer.
transformation: Derive a fixed-k logarithmic window bound, choose k from epsilon, and absorb the remaining constants into B(epsilon,c,v).
observable_controlled: The maximum length of a zero window in the support-coefficient sequence under rationality.
proves_when_hypotheses_hold: For each support and rational presentation satisfying the hypotheses, every zero window is o(log N).
sharp_failures: supportCoeffZeroWindow_length_le_eps_logb_add has a constant that grows rapidly as epsilon shrinks, so it supplies no useful bounded-N exclusion.

human_name: Greedy residual equals the unused Mersenne tail
claim_ceiling: Greedy representation and membership consistency only; the half-value orbit and universal Erdős #257 remain open.
core_idea: The greedy choice is correct exactly while the current residual can still be paid by the remaining tail; for an encoded support the residual is the value of its unprocessed suffix.
invariant: After every finite prefix, chosen-prefix value plus residual equals the target, and the residual equals the suffix value for normalized support inputs.
transformation: Iterate the include-or-skip rule and compare each residual with the exact remaining Mersenne tail.
observable_controlled: Membership in the achievement set and recovery of the representing support.
proves_when_hypotheses_hold: Membership is equivalent to survival at every stage, and the greedy run recovers the original support.
sharp_failures: Z12::half_membership_iff_infinite_greedy_skips leaves both sides open; the invariant re-expresses half membership but does not decide the orbit.

human_name: Nested cylinder stages determine achievement-set measure
claim_ceiling: Lebesgue measure only; nowhere density and total disconnectedness require separate topological mechanisms.
core_idea: Approximate the achievement set by decreasing finite unions of disjoint translated tail intervals whose volumes are exactly computable.
invariant: The depth-d stage is a disjoint union of 2^d cylinders, and the achievement set is their decreasing intersection.
transformation: Compute each finite-stage volume and pass to the intersection by continuity from above.
observable_controlled: Lebesgue measure of the Mersenne achievement set.
proves_when_hypotheses_hold: The finite-stage volumes converge to one, so the achievement set has measure exactly one.
sharp_failures: Z12::mersenne_achievement_set_measure_one controls measure only; nowhere density and total disconnectedness need separate topology evidence.

human_name: First differing digit dominates every later digit
claim_ceiling: Injectivity for digit strings supported in one prescribed offset set; not a classification of arbitrary achievement-set membership.
core_idea: At the first index where two supported binary digit strings differ, that Mersenne weight is strictly larger than the sum of all permitted later weights.
invariant: Strict superincreasingness is hereditary under restriction to any prescribed offset set.
transformation: Cancel the common prefix and compare the first unequal digit with the entire remaining supported tail.
observable_controlled: Injectivity of restricted Mersenne digit coding.
proves_when_hypotheses_hold: Distinct digit strings supported in the same offset set have distinct achievement values.
sharp_failures: supportedMersenneDigitValue_injective depends on strict tail domination; a merely summable or non-strict weight sequence is outside this mechanism.
